[h1]In-Depth[/h1]
[h3]Writing & Worldbuilding[/h3]
Set on a fictional earthlike planet, EFD puts you in the shoes of one of those that survived The Storm, an apocalyptic event that released exotic energy and matter everywhere. Your objective is simple, but difficult at the same time: find a way to escape the doomed planet before the lethal storms lay waste to all. Extraction shooters don’t use narrative or lore depth as strong points; Duckov isn’t an exception, despite a good number of decently-written lore files and dialogues that reveal much about past events. This isn’t a game you’ll play for the story, and it’s not a tale you’ll remember or write your friends about—and that’s fine.

The cartoonish, relatively low-poly style of EFD doesn’t leave much room for intricate worldbuilding or complex indirect narration in its environments; despite that, each area is crafted with enough care to not just like a random bunch of models crammed together, and it can, at times, have some highlight moments from its ambience and mood. Just don’t expect the gritty realism of Tarkov here, or any gritty realism in general at any point, because that’s just not what this game aims for.

[h3]Exploration & Secrets[/h3]
You’ll explore on foot, with the aid of a full map that you can customize with unlimited markers. The first few areas are large, but manageable, while latter ones are downright enormous, and will require several raids to even get a basic lay of the land and its threats. Unlike in other extraction shooters, there’s no extraction timer, so you can stay as much as your food and water supplies allow you to. As you progress, you’ll be able to unlock Beacons, essential fast travel tools to skip earlier maps and instantly start raids in later ones to save time, although some quests will still require you to walk between each or collect one-time use keys to transit to specific areas. Exploration feels generally tense and enjoyable, especially when you reach a new map that has much tougher enemies and yet-unknown bosses, but also better loot.

There’s a multitude of secret areas, many of which require specific items, interactions, weather conditions or times of the day to access. They usually grant unique blueprints, items and other special rewards you can’t obtain in any other way. Keeping track of areas locked out to you, and then coming back once you figured out how to access them, adds another layer of depth to the exploration component. 

[h3]Combat System & Bosses[/h3]
In EFD, fights play out in third person, using a wide range of firearms that range from simple shotguns to fully-modded rifles, and even more exotic ones such as energy guns, without forgetting a variety of grenades for crowd control. The time to kill both for you and the enemy is short at a base level, but is heavily influenced by armor level, which makes lower level ammunition deal considerably less damage, other than specific resistances a character may possess. Because of its camera view, headshots work in a rather peculiar way: you’ll have to hover the mouse exactly on an enemy’s head (or what you think is their head, anyway), to land a critical hit with enhanced damage. 

Compared to other extraction shooters, there’s emphasis on various types of elemental damage, such as fire, poison and electrical, which can be tremendously effective against specific enemies, despite there being no way to tell which enemy is weak against what other than trying your luck and finding out. Melee weapons have their uses, but they’re very niche and often a death sentence in normal combat scenarios. Enemies in EFD aren’t as lethal as in, say, the original Tarkov, but they make that up with numbers, while bosses are their own beast, and some can outright one-shot the unprepared. As customary for the genre, preparation is essential, so having the best weapons and ammunition for the enemies you’re looking for is the key to get out of combat alive. Usually, the trial and error process involves many deaths, after which you may lose all your equipment if you die again while trying to get it back.

[h3]Crafting & Progression[/h3]
Your customizable base, The Bunker, will be populated with new NPCs, facilities and crafting tables as you progress through the quests. These characters not only will give you more tasks and enable you to access better and more gear for purchase, but also directly influence your character’s abilities and skills, acting as trainers. Other than that, you’ll always be able to use the central core of your base to enhance your character’s skills and attributes through a fixed skill tree that progressively requires more money and rarer materials. While crafting is useful, you’ll mostly be able to find everything you need by looting during raids or buying it for cash, with only some exceptions to this rule. I found it rather silly that there are waiting times for upgrades in a single-player game: having to wait, let’s say, one real-life hour for a storage expansion makes little sense in gameplay terms. Weapon modding is basic, and simply consists of dragging whatever compatible attachment straight into your gun, without any further complexity to it, while there’s no modding options for anything else, including plate carriers or helmets.

Short Review
	•	I enjoyed the game and spent many hours playing it.
	•	Recent issues around mods and official moderation permanently changed the experience.
	•	Harmful behavior was tolerated at first, then handled in a rushed and blanket manner that hurt many innocent players and mod creators.
	•	The game now feels unstable and unpleasant rather than fun.

Conclusion
	•	I no longer enjoy playing it and won’t return.
	•	In its current state, I can’t recommend this game.

不推荐。理由不是游戏质量，而是其放任并纵容恶意 Mod 行为。

作为一款 Steam 游戏，其 Mod 生态中出现了极其恶劣、违反社区基本共识的行为：
有 Mod 作者在 Mod 中暗中植入黑名单机制，在玩家进入游戏时检测 Steam ID，一旦命中黑名单就强制退出游戏，且没有任何提示或告知。

这已经不只是“作者个人脾气问题”，而是实质性的恶意代码行为。

更荒谬的是，该黑名单的触发标准完全不透明且极端随意：
有玩家仅仅是在评论区正常反馈 Bug、没有任何攻击性言论，就被作者嫌烦并加入黑名单。

在源代码被社区扒出后，该作者：

公开承认该功能存在

坚称自己“没有任何问题”

对提出质疑的玩家进行人身攻击

其小团体成员甚至公开辱骂玩家，并扬言将来要在创意工坊上传带病毒的 Mod

这些言论和行为都有公开记录。

更令人失望的是官方态度。
在其他游戏（例如 RimWorld）中，官方曾直接介入并下架类似恶意 Mod。但在本作中，有玩家联系官方后发现：

官方对该 Mod 作者极其尊敬，以“老师”相称

还向作者赠送周边礼物

仅以“建议”的口吻要求其修改内容

同时却在社区对玩家表示“官方已要求作者移除恶意代码”

而这些前后不一致的态度，正是 Mod 作者本人因为坐不住而晒出的聊天截图所证实的。

总结一句话：

如果你打算购买这款游戏，请明白：
你不仅是在买游戏本体，也是在默认接受一个官方选择纵容恶意 Mod 行为的生态环境。

如果你在意：

玩家最基本的使用权

Mod 的透明性与安全性

官方是否真正站在玩家一边

那请在入手前三思。

English Review
Not recommended — not because of the game itself, but because of how malicious mod behavior is tolerated and enabled.

Within this game’s mod ecosystem, there exists severely unethical behavior that violates basic modding community norms.

A mod author secretly embedded a blacklist system into their mod.
When the game launches, it checks the player’s Steam ID, and if the ID is on the blacklist, the game is forcibly closed without any warning or notification.

This is not “author preference” — this is deliberate malicious code.

What makes it worse is how arbitrary the blacklist is:
Players have been added simply for politely reporting bugs, with no harassment or hostile language involved — merely because the author found them “annoying”.

After the source code was publicly exposed, the author:

Openly admitted the blacklist existed

Claimed they had done nothing wrong

Personally attacked critics

And members of their inner circle publicly insulted players and even threatened to upload malware mods in the future

All of this happened publicly and is well-documented.

The most disappointing part is the developer’s response.

In other communities (e.g. RimWorld), developers have directly intervened and removed malicious mods.
Here, however, players who contacted the devs found that:

The mod author was treated with excessive deference (addressed as a “respected teacher”)

The author reportedly received official merchandise gifts

The devs only made polite suggestions instead of taking action

While simultaneously telling the community that “the developer has requested the removal of malicious code”

This contradiction was later confirmed by the mod author themselves, who leaked the chat screenshots.

In short:

Buying this game also means accepting an ecosystem where
malicious mod behavior is tolerated and effectively protected.

If you care about:

Basic player rights

Mod transparency and safety

Developers genuinely standing with players

Then please think carefully before purchasing.
